chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: Opening Minton's Playhouse with Henry Minton
summary: As Henry Minton, the first black delegate in Local 802, opened the Playhouse, Caldwell put in a group with Pop Foster, Andy Anderson and pianist Babe Salters.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah, I don't know what that is. Maybe a mistake, Well, (unintelligible). But anyway, now, then you go to Minton's in 1941.
Well, had Minton's been operating before that?
No, he was -- see, he was our first Negro delegate in Local 802. Yes, he was the first one.

The old man played saxophone. Uh-huh, he played saxophone and clarinet. And when he was a delegate, he took a great liking to me because he was a member of this lodge before I got in there. It was all the old timers. So this time -- entertainers, musicians, all the greatest belonged to that lodge. That's why they call it the Musician's Lodge, because so many of the guys belonged to it before I got there.
And when he opened up the Playhouse, when he called me to put the group in there, and being close with him, I put the group, and I had Pop Foster on bass and Andy Anderson on guitar --
Andy Anderson, he used to work with Blanche Calloway, on guitar, and Babe Salters on piano, and I was on tenor, didn't have no drums.
Salters, he was a kid from Chicago. We went to grammar school together.

Very nice piano player. I was surprised because Babe was a very good basketball player. We -- all the kids came along playing basketball, and he must have studied after I left Chicago because Cassino Simpson and all of us guys went to school together. But Babe, we all went to school together too. But Babe wasn't in music at that particular time.

So when he came to New York, I was surprised at him because then he started looking for me. So then I found out he was a little, nice piano player. So I said, okay, Babe, let's go on down and open up at the Playhouse.
